title: Banach algebra of restricted power series at an arbitrary positive real radius
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value, meaning $|a|\ge0$, $|a|=0\Leftrightarrow a=0$, $|1|=1$, $|ab|=|a||b|$ and $|a+b|\le\max(|a|,|b|)$. Suppose the metric $|a-b|$ is complete. For any real $s>0$, let $D_s(F)$ consist of formal series $f=\sum_{n\ge0}a_nW^n$ with $|a_n|s^n\to0$. Equip it with coefficientwise addition, constant scalar multiplication, and Cauchy multiplication $(fg)_n=\sum_{i=0}^n a_i b_{n-i}$. These operations make $D_s(F)$ a unital commutative $F$-algebra. Its finite-valued norm $\|f\|_s=\sup_{n\ge0}|a_n|s^n$ satisfies $\|f\|_s=0\Leftrightarrow f=0$, $\|-f\|_s=\|f\|_s$, $\|1\|_s=1$, $\|af\|_s=|a|\|f\|_s$, $\|f+g\|_s\le\max(\|f\|_s,\|g\|_s)$ and $\|fg\|_s\le\|f\|_s\|g\|_s$. The metric $\|f-g\|_s$ is complete. The constant-coefficient map $\epsilon:D_s(F)\to F$, $\epsilon(f)=a_0$, is a unital $F$-algebra homomorphism with $|\epsilon(f)|\le\|f\|_s$. Constants have norm $|a|$, and $\|W\|_s=s$.
